# Campaign Mode Overview

### Historical Background

Two options in place: 

1. 150th Rifle Division, 79th Rifle Corps, 3rd Shock Army, 1st Belorussian Front: from Pskov to Berlin.  
2. 39th Guards Rifle Division, 8th Guards Army, 3rd Ukrainian Front (later reassigned to 1st Belorussian Front) : From Dnieper (October 1943\) to Berlin (May 1945\) 

My personal preference is the second choice, following the 8th Guards Army from Dnieper to Berlin. More specifically, I’m thinking about the 117th Guards Rifle Regiment.

Finalised version: 117th Guards Rifle Regiment, 39th Guards Rifle Division  
[https\://pamyat-naroda.ru/warunit/id10792/](https://pamyat-naroda.ru/warunit/id10792/) (Div.) and [https\://pamyat-naroda.ru/warunit/id14554/](https://pamyat-naroda.ru/warunit/id14554/) (Polk.)

**Generic Design Ideas**  
Rapid soldier XP progression in Eastern Front mod? XP gain is quicker, but in return veterancy saves are harder to obtain (e.g. taking like 15 instead of 10 patrols to gain the second vet save). This allows the player to experience across the classes and their respective weapons and skills quicker, and also reflect the very high casualty turnover rate in Eastern Front.

Historical evidence for the classes:  
**Assault Sapper**: 11th Assault Engineer-Sapper Brigade (11-я штурмовая инженерно-сапёрная бригада) attatched to the 3rd Ukrainian Front; 1st Assault Engineer-Sapper Brigade (1-я штурмовая инженерно-сапёрная бригада)  attatched to the 1st Belorussian Front, as the 39th Guards Rifles was reassigned to 1st Belorussian Front with the 8th Guards Army.

**OMSBON:** probably as fictional as British-trained commandos of the 29th Inf in vanilla game  
	it’s fine: *all games are historically wrong, but some are fun.*  
***another possibility: Osnaz*** **\-** 273rd Separate Motorised Special Purpose Battalion (**273-й омб ОСНАЗ)** they were actually with the 8th Guards Army.  
**Diversant:** same as above but we keep it for gameplay purpose

# Battle Conditions

### **Renames**

1\. Good coffee \=\> **Inspiring speech** (same effect but different description, something like “Our zampolit had been doing quite a lot of good work for the company’s morale recently, and after today’s speech the boys feel real inspired to show their resolve in combat”)

2.Gerhardt's Pressure \=\> **To the West\!** “Komdiv has issued a new directive, pressuring us to exploit the recent breakthrough and seize the next objective \- now”

3\. Eastern Front Veterans \=\> **Hardened Veterans** “The troops we are going to be facing have been fighting for a while and are well accustomed to combat, evidence suggests that they are even using captured equipment against us.”

4.K-Rations \=\> **Spoiled Provisions** “Unfortunately our provisions have spoiled and those that didn't are neither appetising nor enough for the men” 

5\. Pin Up \- **Liberated Liquor**. The boys have captured some German schnapps. Spirits are high, and bottles are empty\! \+100XP to the Player. Za zdorovye\!

6\. **On Site Acquisition** \- Comrades, the 45th Separate Guards Sapper Battalion found an enemy weapon cache while clearing mines. They were kind enough to drop us a crate. 1 spotted German [weapon crate](https://urb-games.fandom.com/wiki/Weapons_Crate) at the starting line. 

7\. **Failing Industry** “Thanks to the bombing efforts of our Western Allies, the Fascists will receive less supplies than usual. Axis troops have 10% less chance of having special equipment on this map\!” 

8\. **Industrialism:** "Fresh supplies from our Western allies have arrived. Courtesy of Uncle Sam\!"

10\. **Compromised Lines “**Recon reports that enemy infiltration units have exploited a gap in our lines and may operate in your vicinity.”

11\. **The Crucible** “The Enemy is trying to repeat what they did in 1941 and deployed Brandenburgers behind our lines, command wants us to deal with them immediately”

13\. **Vulture's Nest  “**The enemy has set up an HQ right where we are going to be advancing. This is an excellent opportunity to neutralise their leadership and capture valuable intel” (probably should be tweaked to either use a different building sprite or have it randomised, not a lot of manors were still manors in USSR) 

12\. **Secondary Duties** "Friendly troops have been cut off ahead and are in urgent need of supplies and we are gonna be the ones to deliver them”

13\. Last of the Luftwaffe \=\> **Aces of Luftwaffe** “Enemy has deployed some particularly skilled pilots to our sector, and the frontal aviation is having a hard time. Even worse, they seem to be closely cooperating with their ground elements”

14\. Voluntold \- **Subbotnik?** *e.g. “One of our comrades has recently returned from assignment to a ‘volunteer’ debris clearing detail. As a result, his patriotic zeal has been somewhat tempered but he gained some work experience.”*

15\. Air Superiority \- **Free Hunters \-** "The aces of the 176th Guards Fighter Regiment are out hunting down on the Luftwaffe. 10% for Axis air support to be cancelled**”**

16\. Tip of the Spear \-  **Advanced Guard** \- We are spearheading the breakthrough, smashing through enemy lines ahead of the main forces. The Germans are throwing everything they have at us\! \+1 enemy for every day ahead of schedule.

### **Reworks**

1. **Replacements** (Soviets didn't really use the same casualty replacement system as the US so i think we can do smth different with it)

2. **Air Superiority** (subject to change)  
   **Contested Airspace:** like barrage but with planes… forces from both sides will randomly strafe or strike troops? (Could also be a replacement/reword of Mavericks)  
     
3. **H-Hour** (Its a really cool BC, but considering that VDV has a much smaller prevalence while river crossings having a much bigger one, we may need to think of smth a bit different)

4. Gravy Train \- **Armed Resupply** Uncharacteristically, Supply is quite efficient today and delivering goods directly to our frontlines. The tractors can also provide some direct combat support.  
- A T-20 Komsomolets replaces the M29 Wiesel  
- Will stick around to support the squad (until timer elapses)

there was the failed dnieper airborne operation, but after that there were virtually no more paradropping

5. **Standardisation:** Marshal Voroshilov’s Trophy Committee is cracking down on trophy hunters. So turn in your German guns, comrades\! Non-standard weapons are replaced with Soviet-issue equipment.

- SVT-40 for rifle, medic, officer, fire observer, and sniper  
- PPS for avtomatchik, razvedchik, assault sapper, osnaz  
- DP for gunner  
- Diversant class is immune to this effect

### **New ones**

1. **Cocktail Party** (I know the name doesn't really work with the renamed item, but the pun is too fun to pass up)  (Spawns one/several ~~molotovs~~  fire bottles) “We have received a slight excess of gasoline in the latest supply shipment, it was collectively decided to weaponise it” 

2. **Fistful of Fausts** “In line with directives from Front command, we have secured an unopened crate of Faustpatrons. Make good use of them\!” A crate with four panzerfausts will spawn at the start line.   
     
3. **Traitors**. (name subject to more working)  
   **ROA** (not RONA) \- Oder River, 11 Apr 1945; 3 days  
- Maybe also a similar one where its the foreign troops (Romanians?)  
- idea: ROA / Romanian (Hungarians were seen as quite reliable tho probably not them), so basically any enemy that are unreliable and may make use of actionable intel. Maybe spawn an actionable intel somewhere?  
- on the other hand more enemy will spawn in this map


4. **Rasputitsa**  
   The seasonal rains have turned the roads into a muddy mess. The Germans aren’t going anywhere fast, and neither are we. Expect plenty of mud on the battlefield.  
     
- Heavy Clouds BC but for vehicles: disable most vehicle supports on both sides.  
- Exceptions: Kettenkrad, horse carts, T-20 Komsomolets 

5. **Sperrverband** “Enemy has assembled a detachment to cover the retreat of the main force. The detachment seems to contain the leftovers from all kinds of units, all shaken from the previous battle” (Randomised chance for almost any German units to appear, meaning higher chance of SS and FJ, but they all gain a morale penalty)  
     
6. **Preliminary Bombardment** “Corps Artillery will conduct Preliminary Bombardment to soften up the enemy and assist our advance” (Second half of the map receives 2-3 barrages at the beginning of the patrol, locations are random)

7. **Air Resupply** “Fascists are supplying one of their cut-off units by air. We have an opportunity to capture and “redistribute” those supplies if they haven't got to them first.” (Spawns several supply crates on the map, close to enemy positions, chance for a supply drop on enemy lines to occur during gameplay

8. **Regimental Armourers \-** The regiment’s repair workshop is working overtime, turning captured German guns to a serviceable grade. 20% of German weapons on this map become lootable.

9. **Ugly Ducklings** “Friendly tank units operating in the area are still using older vehicles, which negatively impacts their combat performance” (Friendly tanks have less HP, are slower and do less damage with main guns)  
     
10. **Come and See** \- Our forward scouts report German SS and police units operating in the area. No movement can be seen. Thick black smoke rises from the village ahead, but it doesn’t look like that they come from chimneys  
- spawn flames and village of ruined houses at random position on map  
- Friendly Morale \-15%  
- However the hatred of invaders drive our soldiers too: \+15% pin resistance

### **Weapon Text**

weaponText\_mosin \= "Mosin M91/30, the standard-issue rifle of the Red Army. Excellent range and damage, but heavy and slow to fire."  
weaponText\_mosin38 \= "Mosin M38 carbine, a shorter and lighter version of the M91/30."  
weaponText\_mosin44 \= "Mosin M44 carbine, slightly heavier than Mosin M38 due to the integrated folding bayonet.”  
weaponText\_berdan \= "Berdan II, an obsolete single-shot rifle found among Partizans. Fires a powerful black-powder cartridge, but requires reloading after every shot."  
weaponText\_mosinBramit \= "Mosin M91/30 fitted with a Bramit suppressor. Reduced-velocity ammunition softens recoil, at the cost of range and damage."  
weaponText\_svt38 \= "SVT-38, early Soviet semi-automatic rifle. Powerful at medium range, but suffers reliability issues and has an unwieldy centre of mass."  
weaponText\_svt40 \= "SVT-40, improved Soviet semi-automatic rifle. Lighter and more reliable, with improved range."  
weaponText\_avs36 \= "AVS-36, early Soviet automatic rifle with 15-round magazine. Powerful shots and rapid bursts, but prone to stoppages and almost uncontrollable recoil."  
weaponText\_avt40 \= "AVT-40, full-auto SVT-40 with a rare 20-round magazine. Greater range and capacity than the AVS-36, with improved handling and reliability."  
weaponText\_ppd \= "PPD, early Soviet submachine gun with a 25-round box magazine. Frequent reloads due to high rate of fire and relatively small magazine capacity."  
weaponText\_pps \= "PPS, mass-produced lightweight submachine gun with 35-round magazine. Easy to handle and reliable, with a moderate firing rate."  
weaponText\_ppshBox \= "PPSh with a 35-round box magazine. Rapid fire and good close-range damage, with less bulk and better reliability than the drum version."  
weaponText\_ppsh \= "PPSh with its iconic drum. Sustained close-range fire, at the cost of greater bulk and more frequent stoppages."  
weaponText\_ppshObrez \= "PPSh Obrez, used by partisans in concealed carry. Sacrifices range and damage for extremely low bulk.”  
weaponText\_mosinBramit \= "Mosin M91/30 fitted with a Bramit suppressor. Reduced-velocity ammunition softens recoil, at the cost of range and damage."  
weaponText\_ppdBramit \= "PPD fitted with a Bramit suppressor and a 25-round box magazine. Fast, low-recoil fire at close range, but limited capacity and reduced damage."  
weaponText\_ppdBramitDrum \= "PPD fitted with a Bramit suppressor and a drum. Ample ammunition for silent close-range fire, but bulkier and more prone to stoppages due to drum feed."  
weaponText\_dp \= "DP, Degtyarev light machine gun fed by a distinctive 47-round pan magazine. Good range and magazine capacity, but prone to feed issues and recoil spring overheating."  
weaponText\_dpm \= "DPM, Degtyarev light machine gun improved with a redesigned recoil spring arrangement for greater reliability and a pistol grip for better handling."  
weaponText\_dt \= "DT, compact Degtyarev tank machine gun adapted for infantry use. A 63-round pan provides extended fire, while the retractable stock and pistol grip improve handling."  
weaponText\_mosinSelected \= "A carefully selected and maintained Mosin M91/30 issued to a marksman. Excellent range, powerful shots, and dependable operation."  
weaponText\_scopedMosin \= "Scoped M91/30, fitted with a 3.5x PU telescopic sight. Excellent range and damage, but heavy and slow to handle."  
weaponText\_scopedSvt40 \= "Scoped SVT-40, fitted with a 3.5x PU telescopic sight. Allows rapid follow-up shots, trading some long-range precision for greater firepower."  
weaponText\_scopedMosinPE \= "Mosin M91/30, fitted with the more delicate 4x PE telescopic sight. Outstanding range and damage, but heavy to handle and limited to five rounds."  
weaponText\_ptrd \= "PTRD, single-shot 14.5mm anti-tank rifle. Excellent range and damage, but extremely cumbersome and requires reloading after every shot."  
weaponText\_ptrs \= "PTRS, semi-automatic 14.5mm anti-tank rifle with a five-round magazine. Powerful shots and rapid follow-up fire, but even heavier than the PTRD."  
weaponText\_tozB \= "TOZ-B, double-barrel hunting shotgun, now primarily used by partisans. Close-range little wonder and capable of a quick second shot.”  
weaponText\_as44 \= "AS-44, prototype 7.62x39mm Sudayev assault rifle with a 30-round magazine. Good range and steady automatic fire, but heavy and slow to handle."  
weaponText\_rd44 \= "RD-44, prototype 7.62x39mm Degtyarev machine gun. Very good payload (100), with manageable recoil and reduced range and damage."  
weaponText\_rp46 \= "Degtyarev DP with experimental belt-feed mechanism. Excellent payload (250-round belt), but cumbersome and prone to feed stoppages."

# Items

# Grenades

**Molotov** → Incendiary Bottle

**RGD-33 bundled grenade?** 

- like vanilla AT grenade but different sprite?   
- Also less powerful but longer range since mostly contained just 3 RGDs, oh and also more fragmentation range? (RGD had a frag sleeve but it was removable, idk)  
- I’d say leave frag to F-1s.   
  - Also RGD-33 was complicated as hell to use, maybe an exp check for throwing.   
  - Or we just don’t include the base RGD-33 in the mod because this thing was already hugely unpopular and by 1943-44 it was largely replaced by the RG-42 (and good old F-1)

**RPG-40** for some short range big explosions. They were not really good for AT purposes but did pack a serious amount of HE explosives.

- 20m throw range; 20m fragmentation range  
- will probably track a tank if close enough  
- opposite of vanilla impact nade: this thing is short-range, large radius  
- basically hand-thrown satchel charge  
- give to the **Assault Sapper**

**![][image1]**  
**RG-42**

- offensive nade: longer range  
- blast damage \- less deadly  
- give to the **Avtomatchiki**

**F-1**

- defensive: less range (vanilla frag)  
- frag damage with a good radius  
- give to the **Strelok**

 

**Contact grenade should be removed**

- neither Soviets, nor Germans used those (iirc only AT grenades had impact fuses),   
- **Bangalore too**

273-й омб ОСНАЗ форсировал реку Даме даже на день раньше своих коллег из 274-го. Первая группа, захватив плацдарм, удержала его, пока амфибии переправляли следом два полка 27-й сд. Вторая группа сделала то же самое в районе Грюнау, захватив плацдарм, расширив его и переправив следом части 12-й сд. В следующие дни, пока сапёрные части не навели переправы, «форды-амфибии» таскали через реку паромы с бойцами и грузами.
